chief_complaint: Stage 2 hypertension with uncontrolled blood pressure (SBP 159 / DBP 112) noted on latest vitals
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 58‑year‑old man with chronic HIV infection diagnosed in 2003, maintained on a boosted protease‑inhibitor regimen (lamivudine/tenofovir, darunavir, ritonavir). He has longstanding obesity (BMI ≥30 since 2000) and developed prediabetes (A1c 5.9%) and anemia in 2008. Obstructive sleep apnea was diagnosed in early 2018, but no CPAP therapy is documented. Blood pressure measurements indicate stage 2 hypertension, yet no antihypertensive agents are prescribed. Socially, he transitioned from full‑time to part‑time employment in 2018, reports ongoing environmental violence and chronic stress, and has only a high‑school education. The last recorded clinical encounter was in January 2019, suggesting limited recent engagement with care.

past_medical_history: Appendectomy (1984). Prior full‑time employment (resolved 2018). Resolved social isolation (2018). Two resolved medication‑review reminders (2017, 2018). Minor lacerations of hand and other sites resolved in 2018.

risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular risk is elevated due to stage 2 hypertension, obesity, HIV‑associated inflammation, and probable dyslipidaemia from protease‑inhibitor therapy. Metabolic risk includes prediabetes and insulin resistance. Renal risk is present from hypertension, HIV, and tenofovir exposure, but eGFR and proteinuria data are missing. Anemia may reflect chronic disease or renal insufficiency. Obstructive sleep apnea further worsens blood pressure and metabolic control. Psychosocial stressors and socioeconomic instability increase the likelihood of poor adherence and delayed care.

Renal function (eGFR) not recorded; important given tenofovir exposure and hypertension.
Lipid panel absent; needed to assess cardiovascular risk and ART‑related dyslipidaemia.
No antihypertensive agents documented despite stage 2 hypertension.
No CPAP or other OSA treatment recorded.
Family history of cardiovascular disease not provided.
No clinical encounters after 2019‑01‑07; data may be outdated for current management.

clinical_impression: Middle‑aged man with chronic HIV infection on a boosted protease‑inhibitor regimen, complicated by multiple metabolic and cardiovascular risk factors (stage 2 hypertension, obesity, prediabetes, OSA) and anemia. Social stressors and limited recent healthcare contact raise concern for suboptimal disease control and heightened risk of cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic complications.
